description: Sets of need-ranges a requester MUST refuse, each with the rule it breaks in `reason` and the category of refusal in `error`: ranges that touch or overlap, ranges out of order, an empty range, a range that ends past the largest offset, bytes after the message, a count that is not its shortest varint, a varint that runs past ten bytes, and a count the message does not hold

cases.name: the second range starts where the first ends
cases.reason: the ranges touch, and one set of needed bytes has one form

cases.name: the second range starts before the first ends
cases.reason: the ranges overlap, and a byte is named twice

cases.name: the ranges are not ascending
cases.reason: a later range starts before an earlier one

cases.name: a range of no bytes
cases.reason: a range that asks for nothing

cases.name: a range that ends past the largest offset
cases.reason: the start and the length add up to past the largest offset a u64 holds

cases.name: one byte after the message
cases.reason: bytes follow the count the message declares

cases.name: a count that is not its shortest varint
cases.reason: the count 1 is written in two bytes, so the message has two spellings

cases.name: a varint that runs past ten bytes
cases.reason: a varint of a u64 is at most ten bytes long, and the bytes after it do not make it one

cases.name: a count the message does not hold
cases.reason: the message ends before the second range
